title: LEFT JOIN
description: A LEFT JOIN keeps every row from the left table, even if nothing matches on the right - the unmatched columns just come back as NULL. Write a query that returns every customer's `first_name` alongside the `id` of any order they've placed, including customers who have never ordered (their order id should be NULL).
hints: 💡 SQL concept to consider: LEFT JOIN

LEFT JOIN customers TO orders keeps every customer row no matter what - if a customer has no matching order, orders.id just comes back NULL instead of the row disappearing the way it would with an INNER JOIN.
Select customers.first_name and orders.id, using LEFT JOIN orders ON customers.id = orders.customer_id (customers on the left).
expected_behavior: Returns one row per customer - customers with orders get one row per order, customers with none get a single row with a NULL order id.
solution: SELECT customers.first_name, orders.id FROM customers LEFT JOIN orders ON customers.id = orders.customer_id;
explanation: LEFT JOIN is INNER JOIN plus "and keep unmatched left rows too, padded with NULLs" - reach for it whenever the left table's rows all matter, whether or not they have a match.
postgres_note: LEFT OUTER JOIN and LEFT JOIN are exactly the same thing in Postgres - OUTER is optional and rarely written.
